gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 70mai's own US store sells the non-Ultra 70mai A900 at $159.00 on 2026-11-21. 70mai lists it as true 4K HDR on both front and rear at 30 fps. That is less than half the $409.99 VIOFO charges in its own store for the A229 Ultra 2CH and about a third of the $499.99 A900 Ultra, which are the dual-4K cameras ChatGPT recommended.
standout_why: I compared against two Product Bible pages (Best 4K Dash Cams and Best Front and Rear Dash Cams, both dated 2026-11-19), which ChatGPT cited. Their only priced dual-4K camera is the VIOFO A229 Ultra 2CH ($299.99 at Amazon on Nov 19). They name the BlackVue Elite 10 2CH as dual 4K but give it no price on the front-and-rear page. Neither page lists the 70mai A900, the A900 Ultra, the 70mai T800 or the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K. Neither gives a hardwire-kit price, and neither says whether either channel drops its frame rate when both record. I could not open Car and Driver (fetch refused) or thecargearguide (certificate error), so I can't say what they list. ChatGPT's own answer showed the A229 Ultra at $299.99 (Best Buy) in one chat and $409.99 (VIOFO) in the other, plus the A900 Ultra at $499.99 and the Rexing R88 at $359.99. It never showed a dual-4K camera under $299.99.
decides: The finding doesn't overturn the A229 Ultra as the best-documented dual-4K pick. VIOFO names the same IMX678 sensor in both cameras and HDR on both channels. Its parking hardwire kit, the HK4, is only $17.99, against $129.99 for the 70mai UP12/UP11 kit. What it does is open a budget tier ChatGPT missed: the 70mai A900 at $159.00. The A900's store text says 4K front and rear at 30 fps, but it doesn't name a sensor, so it can win on price but not on documented sensor quality. The Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K, at $239.99 per our partner read of 2026-11-21, would sit between the A900 and the A229 Ultra. That is the Vantrue row that may honestly place in the top three. However, I couldn't open its product page (HTTP 429 on all five tries), so I have no sourced resolution, sensor or frame rate for it. Treat it as unverified until the page is read. If its page confirms 4K on both channels, it belongs in the table as the mid-price pick. If it doesn't, no Vantrue product belongs: the N4 Pro S has a 1440p rear and the N5S a 2592×1944 front, so neither meets the question, and the page should be skipped.
